summary: FinTrust and Redwood discussed data residency and region pinning options. Customer requires EEA-only processing for PII, wants details on cross-border fallbacks, sub-processors, and KMS key custody. Redwood explained hosted vs dedicated/private options, region pinning behavior, audit logs, and encryption at rest/in-transit. transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-03-04 15:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Michael Lopez (FinTrust - Head of Cloud), Sara Nguyen (FinTrust - Security Architect), David Park (FinTrust - Procurement)

00:00 Alex Kim: hey everyone thanks for joining today, appreciate you carving out time. quick agenda, we'll run through your EEA-only requirements, region pinning options, sub-processor list and then drill into KMS and audit logs. priya will cover the architecture details.
00:32 Michael Lopez: yeah thanks alex. high level — FinTrust has regulatory requirement to keep european customer PII processed and stored within the EEA. we also need to know what happens on failover, like if a eu region is unhealthy does traffic go to us, or is it blocked. also curious on sub-processors and whether any cross-border replication occurs.
01:10 Priya Shah: totally understood. quick caveat, i'll describe both hosted and private modes. hosted can be configured for region pinning — we keep inference and storage in a pinned region, however certain control-plane operations may still touch other regions unless we run Private. with Dedicated/Private you can get a stronger isolation.
01:45 Sara Nguyen: can you be specific about control plane? our legal team insists no control-plane metadata leaves the EU for eu accounts.
02:05 Priya Shah: right, so in our Hosted API the control plane is multi-region by default for operational observability — name might be the controlplane — sorry, that's the auto. we do offer a private control-plane option in our Private deployment (customer-managed) where the control plane endpoints are only in the customer's VPC or chosen region. for the hosted offering we have region pinning for data at rest and runtime inference, but some telemetry for health by default could go to other regions unless you opt into private control plane.
02:40 Michael Lopez: ok, so hosted pinned to eu-west-1, but control-plane metadata might briefly route to us-east-1? that's a no go unless it's encrypted and never contains customer PII.
03:05 Alex Kim: yes, exactly. we can share the telemetry/metadata schema. we also have redact options and we don't include customer prompt content in those control plane logs unless explicitly enabled for debugging. the default is minimal metrics.
03:40 David Park: who's the KMS provider? we need customer-managed keys.
04:05 Priya Shah: we support KMS integrations. for hosted you can bring your own key (BYOK) via AWS KMS or GCP KMS, and for Private deployments you can hold the keys in your HSM. note: for BYOK there is an initial key exchange process and we keep encrypted blobs in the eu region when pinned. the private path also supports HSM direct attestations.
04:40 Sara Nguyen: can you confirm that if we choose BYOK with EU-restricted region pinning, the key material is never exported to non-EU regions?
05:05 Priya Shah: yes, that's the design — keys are region-scoped for the customer. Redwood stores wrapped keys and the master key material remains with the customer's KMS in the region; the runtime uses the KMS endpoint in the pinned region. in hosted we call the kms endpoint in the same region. there is no automatic cross-region key export.
05:40 Michael Lopez: about cross-border processing: what about background model updates, telemetry or managed backups? are those replicated to the us for disaster recovery?
06:10 Alex Kim: backups by default are region-local for pinned deployments. for high availability we offer geo-replication as an opt-in feature and that would be explicitly documented in the DPA. by default, EU-pinned workloads remain in EU.
06:35 Sara Nguyen: okay, what's the sub-processor list? specifically any US-based sub-processors that touch unredacted data?
07:00 Priya Shah: our typical sub-processors (high level) include cloud infra providers like AWS and GCP, and analytics providers for anonymized usage metrics. we will send the up-to-date sub-processor list; importantly we redact PII from analytics. there are rare cases where SREs may access redacted debug artifacts under NDA for emergency debugging and that is auditable.
07:35 Michael Lopez: will you provide SOC 2 and ISO artifacts? our procurement needs SOC 2 Type II and preferably ISO 27001.
transcript_continued:
08:02 Alex Kim: yes, we have SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001. we'll send the reports; there are redacted versions for public sharing and fully redacted ones under NDA. we'll also include our sub-processor list and DPA template.
08:40 Sara Nguyen: audit logs and retention — can we define retention periods and export logs to our SIEM?
09:05 Priya Shah: we expose audit logs (admin ops, access events, API calls) for the tenancy. logs can be configured to ship to a customer-owned S3/GCS bucket in EU region using our log export, and we support syslog/Splunk/Datadog with EU endpoints. retention is configurable; default retention is 90 days but you can set longer or export to your SIEM for long term.
09:40 Michael Lopez: great. about SSO and RBAC — we need SCIM for provisioning and fine grained RBAC.
10:05 Alex Kim: we support SAML SSO + SCIM provisioning and role-based policies. for Private deployments you can hook into your existing IdP over the VPC. we'll provide the RBAC matrix and available roles.
10:30 David Park: procurement question — if we go hosted with EU pinning, what contractual guarantees exist on cross-border fallback?
10:55 Alex Kim: contractual language in the DPA can say no cross-border processing except for operational reasons, and require notice/consent. for stricter needs we recommend Private deployment where you control the control plane.
11:20 Michael Lopez: what's the failure mode — if one EU AZ goes down do you failover within EU or to outside regions?
11:45 Priya Shah: by default we failover within the same region to another AZ. multi-region HA would be an opt-in geo-replication feature — if enabled that's configured to replicate only to EU regions. the automatic global failover to US is not part of our EU-pinning; we'd only do cross-border failover if explicitly enabled in account settings.
12:10 Sara Nguyen: are there any third-party model providers (like models hosted by other vendors) that could introduce cross-border calls?
12:40 Priya Shah: we primarily serve models from our curated catalog, and we have some partnerships. whenever a third-party model is used we document where inference happens. we will not call an external third-party model outside the pinned region unless you allow it. sometimes models are licensed from partners and the runtime may call model-serving endpoints — we include that in the sub-processor and model provenance docs.
13:15 Michael Lopez: ok good. your telemetry schema — does it include any hashes or fingerprints of prompt content that might be reversible?
13:45 Priya Shah: telemetry includes hashed identifiers and aggregated metrics. we use salted non-reversible hashes for trace IDs; prompt content is not stored in telemetry by default. for debugging we can enable debug capture, but it's opt-in and requires consent.
14:10 David Park: can you walk through an actual EU-only architecture? like network flows, VPC peering, private link, etc.
14:40 Priya Shah: sure — (screenshare reference) you run a private VPC in eu-west-1, we establish PrivateLink endpoints or VPC peering; inference nodes and storage are provisioned within your eu VPC or our dedicated eu subnets if using Dedicated. control plane can be deployed into your VPC for Private offering. the important bit: all egress and storage endpoints are eu endpoints. we also offer NAT-less options to avoid unintended egress.
15:25 Michael Lopez: sounds promising. does Redwood run any telemetry that needs a backchannel to a us analytics vendor?
15:50 Alex Kim: not by default; analytics pipeline is region-configurable. any integration with US analytics vendors would be per-customer opt-in and documented.
16:15 Sara Nguyen: what about legal — DPA and SCCs for data transfer?
16:35 Alex Kim: yes DPA includes SCCs where applicable and we provide standard EU addendum for transfers. for customers requiring strictly no transfers we recommend Private on-prem or VPC-hosted options.
17:00 Michael Lopez: on the sub-processor list, do you have any EU hosting-only subcontractors?
17:20 Priya Shah: our infra providers have EU regions; we can provide explicit region-scoped sub-processor entries. we'll flag those who are EU-only.
17:50 David Park: any recent incidents or security notices relevant? we need to log that for procurement risk review.
18:10 Alex Kim: we've had no incidents impacting customer data in the last 24 months; we publish security advisories and will include the timeline and remediation notes.
18:40 Sara Nguyen: encryption in transit — TLS everywhere, mutual TLS for private links?
19:00 Priya Shah: TLS 1.2+ in transit, mTLS for private link/VPC peering. at rest AES-256, keys managed via your KMS if BYOK.
19:25 Michael Lopez: do you support field-level encryption for PII before it hits the model?
19:50 Priya Shah: we support tokenization and client-side encryption approaches; you can encrypt sensitive fields prior to sending. however that can impact model utility. we can work with your data team on recommended patterns.
20:15 David Park: procurement — timeline and pricing implications for Private vs Hosted?
20:35 Alex Kim: Private has a platform fee and longer lead time (network setup, provisioning). Hosted with EU pinning is faster but less strict control plane guarantees. we can provide a comparison spreadsheet.
21:00 Michael Lopez: okay let's summarize next steps.
21:10 Alex Kim: recap: we'll send SOC2/ISO artifacts, sub-processor list, DPA, region-pinning architecture doc, and proposed network deep-dive. priya will draft the architecture note. sara will provide sub-processor requirements and any legal redlines.
21:40 Sara Nguyen: thanks. one more quick question — do you have any EU-based SREs who might access debug logs?
22:05 Priya Shah: we have regional SREs and access is audited; we can provide an access policy and the audit log examples.
22:30 David Park: great. that's all from procurement.
22:40 Alex Kim: thanks everyone; we'll follow up with docs and propose times for the network call.
22:50 Michael Lopez: appreciate it.
23:00 End of recording.

Notes: some transcription errors present (product name variations, minor speaker attribution issues). Links shared: SOC2 link (will be sent via email), DPA template (drive link), region pinning diagram (attachment).
